exampleAnswers.title: Finding a CDF Given a PDF With a Lower Bound

question.text: Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function \[ f(x) = \begin{cases}\dfrac{6}{x^7}, \quad &x \geq 1\\[5pt] 0,\quad &x< 1\end{cases} \] its cumulative distribution function is \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, \quad & x < 1 \\[5pt] h(x) , \quad & x \geq 1. \end{cases} \] Find the function $h(x).$
question.explanation:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $x \geq 1,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

\[ F(x) = P(X \leq x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 1 \\[5pt] \displaystyle \int_1^x f(t) \, \textrm dt, & x \geq 1 \end{cases} \]

For the given probability density function, we have

\[ \begin{align*} \int_{1}^x f(t) \, \textrm dt &= \int_{1}^x \dfrac{6}{t^7} \, \textrm dt \\[5pt]\ &= \left. -\dfrac{1}{t^6} \right|_{1}^x \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{x^6} + 1 \\[5pt] &= 1 - \dfrac{1}{x^6}. \end{align*} \]

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

\[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 1 \\[5pt] \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue} 1 - \dfrac{1}{x^6}} , & x \geq 1. \end{cases} \]

question.text: Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function \[ f(x) = \begin{cases}e^{1-x}, \quad &x \geq 1\\[5pt] 0, \quad &x< 1\end{cases} \] its cumulative distribution function is \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, \quad & x < 1 \\[5pt] h(x) , \quad & x \geq 1. \end{cases} \] Find the function $h(x).$
question.explanation:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $x \geq 1,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form: \[ F(x) = P(X \leq x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 1 \\[5pt] \displaystyle \int_1^x f(t) \, \textrm dt, & x \geq 1 \end{cases} \]

For the given probability density function, we have \begin{align*} \int_{1}^x f(t) \, \textrm dt &= \int_{1}^x e^{1-t} \, \textrm dt \\[5pt]\ &= -e^{1-t} \bigg|_{1}^x \\[5pt] &= -e^{1-x}+ 1 \\[5pt] &= 1 - e^{1-x}. \end{align*}

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x <1 ,\\[5pt] \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}1 - e^{1-x}} , & x \geq 1. \end{cases} \]

question.text:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function
\[
f(x) = \dfrac{e^{-\left|x/4\right|}}{8}, \quad x \in (-\infty, \infty),
\]
its cumulative distribution function is
\[
F(x) = \begin{cases}
h(x), \quad & x < 0 \\[5pt]
1-\dfrac{e^{-x/4}}{2}, \quad & x \geq 0
\end{cases}
\]
where $h(x)=$
question.explanation:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that involves an absolute value, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form: \[ F(x) = P(X \leq x) = \begin{cases} \displaystyle \int_{-\infty}^x \dfrac{e^{t/4}}{8} \, \textrm dt, & x < 0 \\[5pt] \displaystyle \int_{-\infty}^0 \dfrac{e^{t/4}}{8} \, \textrm dt + \int_{0}^x \dfrac{e^{-t/4}}{8} \, \textrm dt, & x \geq 0 \end{cases} \]

Let's compute the integrals.

  • If $x \leq 0,$ we have \[ \begin{align*} \int_{-\infty}^x \dfrac{e^{t/4}}{8} \, \textrm dt &= \left. \dfrac{e^{t/4}}{2} \right|_{-\infty}^x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{e^{x/4}}{2}, \end{align*} \] Therefore, \[ \begin{align*} \int_{-\infty}^0 \dfrac{e^{t/4}}{8} \, \textrm dt &= \left. \dfrac{e^{x/4}}{2} \right|_{x=0} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*} \]

  • If $x > 0,$ we have \[ \begin{align*} \int_{0}^x \dfrac{e^{-t/4}}{8} \, \textrm dt &= -\left. \dfrac{e^{-t/4}}{2} \right|_{0}^x \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{e^{-x/4}}{2} + \dfrac12. \end{align*} \] As a result, we get \[ \begin{align*} \int_{-\infty}^0 \dfrac{e^{-t/4}}{8} \, \textrm dt + \int_{0}^x \dfrac{e^{-t/4}}{8} \, \textrm dt &= \dfrac{1}{2} + \left( -\dfrac{e^{-x/4}}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} \right) \\[5pt] &= 1-\dfrac{e^{-x/4}}{2}. \end{align*} \]

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{e^{x/4}}{2}} , & x < 0 \\[5pt] 1-\dfrac{e^{-x/4}}{2}, & x \geq 0. \end{cases} \]

example.title: Computing a CDF Given a PDF That’s Nonzero Over All Real Numbers

question.text:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function \[ f(x) = \dfrac{6e^{3x}}{\pi(1+e^{6x})}, \quad x \in (-\infty, \infty), \]

find the cumulative distribution function $F(x).$
question.explanation:
The cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

\[ F(x) = P(X \leq x) = \int_{-\infty}^x f(t) \, \textrm dt. \]

For the given probability density function, we have

\[ \begin{align*} F(x) &= \int_{-\infty}^x f(t) \, \textrm dt \\[5pt] &= \int_{-\infty}^x \dfrac{6e^{3t}}{\pi(1+e^{6t})} \, \textrm dt \\[5pt] &= \left. \dfrac{2\arctan e^{3t}}{\pi} \right|_{-\infty}^x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2\arctan e^{3x}}{\pi}. \end{align*} \]

question.text:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function
\[
f(x) = 2e^{-|4x|}, \quad x \in (-\infty, \infty),
\]
its cumulative distribution function is
\[
F(x) =  
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{e^{4x}}{2}, \quad & x \leq 0 \\[5pt] 
h(x), \quad & x \gt 0
\end{cases}
\]
where $h(x)=$
question.explanation:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that involves an absolute value, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form: \[ F(x) = P(X \leq x) = \begin{cases} \displaystyle \int_{-\infty}^x 2e^{4t} \, \textrm dt, & x \leq 0 \\[5pt] \displaystyle \int_{-\infty}^0 2e^{4t} \, \textrm dt + \int_{0}^x 2e^{-4t} \, \textrm dt, & x \gt 0 \end{cases} \]

Let's compute the integrals.

  • If $x \leq 0,$ we have \[ \begin{align*} \int_{-\infty}^x 2e^{4t} \, \textrm dt &= \left. \dfrac{e^{4t}}{2} \right|_{-\infty}^x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{e^{4x}}{2}. \end{align*} \] In particular, \[ \begin{align*} \int_{-\infty}^0 2e^{4t} \, \textrm dt &= \left. \dfrac{e^{4x}}{2} \right|_{x=0} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*} \]

  • If $x \gt 0,$ we have \[ \begin{align*} \int_{0}^x 2e^{-4t} \, \textrm dt &= -\left. \dfrac{e^{-4t}}{2} \right|_{0}^x \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{e^{-4x}}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*} \] As a result, we get \[ \begin{align*} \int_{-\infty}^0 2e^{4t} \, \textrm dt + \int_{0}^x 2e^{-4t} \, \textrm dt &= \dfrac{1}{2} + \left( -\dfrac{e^{-4x}}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} \right) \\[5pt] &= 1 -\dfrac{e^{-4x}}{2}. \end{align*} \]

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{e^{4x}}{2} , \quad & x \leq 0, \\[5pt] \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{1 - \dfrac{e^{-4x}}{2}}, \quad & x \gt 0. \end{cases} \]

 \dfrac{e^{5x}}{2}, \quad & x < 0 \\[5pt]
h(x), \quad & x \geq 0
\end{cases}

Let's compute the integrals.

  • If $x \leq 0,$ we have \[ \begin{align*} \int_{-\infty}^x \dfrac52e^{5t} \, \textrm dt &= \left. \dfrac{e^{5t}}{2} \right|_{-\infty}^x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{e^{5x}}{2}, \end{align*} \] Therefore, \[ \begin{align*} \int_{-\infty}^0 \dfrac52e^{5t} \, \textrm dt &= \left. \dfrac{e^{5x}}{2} \right|_{x=0} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*} \]

  • If $x > 0,$ we have \[ \begin{align*} \int_{0}^x \dfrac52e^{-5t} \, \textrm dt &= -\left. \dfrac{e^{-5t}}{2} \right|_{0}^x \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{e^{-5x}}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*} \] As a result, we get \[ \begin{align*} \int_{-\infty}^0 \dfrac52e^{5t} \, \textrm dt + \int_{0}^x \dfrac52e^{-5t} \, \textrm dt &= \dfrac{1}{2} + \left( -\dfrac{e^{-5x}}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} \right) \\[5pt] &= 1-\dfrac{e^{-5x}}{2}. \end{align*} \]

question.text:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function \[ f(x) = \dfrac{3x^2}{\pi(1+x^6)}, \quad x \in (-\infty, \infty), \]

find the cumulative distribution function $F(x).$
question.explanation:
The cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

\[ F(x) = P(X \leq x) = \int_{-\infty}^x f(t) \, \textrm dt. \]

For the given probability density function, we have

\[ \begin{align*} F(x) &= \int_{-\infty}^x f(t) \, \textrm dt \\[5pt] &= \int_{-\infty}^x \dfrac{3t^2}{\pi(1+t^6)} \, \textrm dt \\[5pt] &= \left. \dfrac{\arctan(t^3)}{\pi} \right|_{-\infty}^x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\arctan(x^3)}{\pi} + \dfrac{1}{2} \end{align*} \]

question.text:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function
\[
f(x) = \begin{cases}\dfrac{2}{33}(2+x) , \quad &2 \leq x \leq 5\\[5pt]
0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise}\end{cases}
\]
its cumulative distribution function is 
\[
F(x) = 
\begin{cases}
0, \quad & x < 2 \\[5pt]
h(x), \quad & 2 \leq x \leq 5\\[5pt]
1, \quad & x > 5
\end{cases}
\]
where $h(x)=$
question.explanation:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $2 \leq x \leq 5,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form: \[ F(x) = P(X \leq x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 2 \\[5pt] \displaystyle \int_2^x f(t) \, \textrm dt, & 2 \leq x \leq 5 \\[5pt] 1, & x > 5 \end{cases} \]

For the given probability density function, we have \[ \begin{align*} \int_{2}^x f(t) \, \textrm dt &= \int_{2}^x \dfrac{2}{33}(2+t) \, \textrm dt \\[5pt]\ &= \left. \left(\dfrac{4}{33}t+\dfrac{t^2}{33}\right) \right|_{2}^x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{x^2}{33}+\dfrac{4x}{33}-\dfrac{12}{33} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{33}(x^2+4x-12) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{33}(x+6)(x-2). \end{align*} \]

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 2 \\[5pt] \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{1}{33}(x+6)(x-2)}, & 2 \leq x \leq 5 \\[5pt] 1, & x > 5. \end{cases} \]

example.title: Finding a CDF Given a PDF With Lower and Upper Bounds

question.text: Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function \[ f(x) = \begin{cases}\dfrac{2}{3} (4-x), \quad &2 \leq x \leq 5\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise}\end{cases} \] its cumulative distribution function is \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, \quad & x < 2 \\[5pt] h(x), \quad & 2 \leq x \leq 5\\[5pt] 1, \quad & x > 5. \end{cases} \] Find the function $h(x).$
question.explanation:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $2 \leq x \leq 5,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form: \[ F(x) = P(X \leq x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 2 \\[5pt] \displaystyle \int_2^x f(t) \, \textrm dt, & 2 \leq x \leq 5 \\[5pt] 1, & x > 5 \end{cases} \]

For the given probability density function, we have \[ \begin{align*} \int_{2}^x f(t) \, \textrm dt &= \int_{2}^x \dfrac{2}{3}(4-t) \, \textrm dt \\[5pt]\ &= \left. -\dfrac{1}{3}t\left(t-8 \right) \right|_{2}^x \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{3}x( x - 8)-4 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-x^2 +8x-12}{3}. \end{align*} \]

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 2 \\[5pt] \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue} \dfrac{-x^2 +8x-12}{3}}, & 2 \leq x \leq 5 \\[5pt] 1, & x > 5. \end{cases} \]

question.text:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 1 \\[5pt] 1 - \dfrac{1}{x^6} , & x \geq 1, \end{cases} \]

find $P(X \leq 2).$
question.explanation:
The cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

\[ F(x) = P(X \leq x). \]

Hence, the required probability is $F(2)=1-\dfrac{1}{2^6}=\dfrac{63}{64}.$

example.title: Computing a Probability Over an Interval Using a CDF

question.text:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 0 \\[3pt] \dfrac x2, & 0\leq x < 2 \\[5pt] 1, & x \geq 2, \\[3pt] \end{cases} \]

find $P(1\leq X \leq 3).$
question.explanation:
Remember that for continuous random variables, it doesn't matter whether or not we include the endpoints of the interval. So we can perform the computation as follows:

\[ \begin{align*} P(1\leq X \leq 3) &= P(1 < X \leq 3) \\[3pt] &=P(X \leq 3)-P(X\leq 1) \\[3pt] &= F(3)-F(1) \\[3pt] &= 1-\dfrac 12 \\[3pt] &= \dfrac12. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Computing a Probability Over an Interval Using a CDF

question.text:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 0 \\[3pt] 1-e^{-x}, & x \geq 0, \end{cases} \]

find $P(X > 2).$
question.explanation:
We can perform this computation using the complement, as follows:

\[ \begin{align*} P(X > 2) &= 1 - P(X \leq 2) \\[3pt] &= 1 - F(2) \\[3pt] &= 1 - (1 - e^{-2}) \\[3pt] &= e^{-2} \\[3pt] &= \dfrac{1}{e^2} \end{align*} \]

example.title: Computing a Probability Over an Interval Using a CDF

question.text:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, \quad &x < 0, \\[3pt] x^2, \quad &0 \leq x \leq 1,\\[3pt] 1, \quad &x > 1, \end{cases} \]

find $P\left(\dfrac 12\lt X \leq 2\right).$
question.explanation:
We can perform this computation as follows:

\[ \begin{align*} P\left(\dfrac 12\lt X \leq 2\right) &= P(X \leq 2)-P\left (X\leq \dfrac12\right) \\[3pt] &= F(2)-F\left(\dfrac12\right) \\[3pt] &=1-\left(\dfrac12\right)^2\\[3pt] &= \dfrac{3}{4}. \end{align*} \]

question.text:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function \[ F(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{e^x}{2} , & x < 0 \\[5pt] 1-\dfrac{e^{-x}}{2}, & x \geq 0, \end{cases} \]

find $P(X \geq 4).$
question.explanation:
Remember that for continuous random variables, it doesn't matter whether or not we include the endpoints of the interval. So we have

\[ P(X \geq 4) =P(X > 4). \]

We can perform this computation using the complement, as follows: \[ \begin{align*} P(X > 4) &= 1 - P(X \leq 4) \\[3pt] &= 1 - F(4) \\[3pt] &= 1 - \left(1-\dfrac{e^{-4}}{2}\right) \\[3pt] &= \dfrac12e^{-4} \\[3pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2e^4} \end{align*} \]
